title: UGC NET Electronic Science Subject Mock Test 2024

questions.question_text: In an n-type semiconductor, the Hall coefficient R_H was measured to be negative. If the magnetic field B is applied along the +z axis and electric current I flows along the +x axis, in which direction will the Hall voltage develop?
questions.explanation: Lorentz force on moving electrons: F = -e (v_x x B_z) = -e (v_x a_x x B_z a_z) = -e v_x (-a_y) = +e v_x a_y. However, because electrons carry negative charge, they drift along -x direction (v_x < 0), forcing electrons toward the -y face, establishing a negative Hall voltage in the -y direction.
questions.numerical_formula: Hall Effect Equation: V_H = (I * B) / (n * q * w), R_H = 1 / (n * q) for electrons.
questions.common_pitfalls: Confusing the deflection direction of electrons vs positive holes under magnetic force.

questions.question_text: An operational amplifier with an open-loop gain of A_OL = 100,000 and input offset voltage V_os = 2 mV is configured as an inverting amplifier with R1 = 10 kOhm and Rf = 100 kOhm. What is the closed-loop voltage gain and output offset voltage?
questions.explanation: Closed-loop inverting gain A_CL = -Rf / R1 = -100 k / 10 k = -10. Output offset voltage due to input offset V_os is magnified by the non-inverting noise gain: V_out,os = V_os * (1 + Rf/R1) = 2 mV * (1 + 10) = 2 mV * 11 = 22 mV.
questions.numerical_formula: Noise Gain A_noise = 1 + (Rf / R1) = 11. Signal Gain A_sig = - (Rf / R1) = -10.
questions.common_pitfalls: Common error: Multiplying input offset by inverting gain (-10) instead of noise gain (11).

questions.question_text: According to the Nyquist Sampling Theorem, what is the minimum sampling rate required to avoid aliasing for a continuous bandpass signal centered at f_c = 100 MHz with a bandwidth B = 20 MHz?
questions.explanation: For bandpass sampling with signal frequencies between f_L = 90 MHz and f_H = 110 MHz, the theoretical minimum sampling rate is 2B = 40 MHz, provided f_s satisfies the integer guard condition: 2f_H / n <= f_s <= 2f_L / (n-1) where n = floor(f_H / B) = floor(110/20) = 5.
questions.numerical_formula: Bandpass sampling theorem: f_s = (2 * f_H) / n where n = floor(f_H / Bandwidth).
questions.common_pitfalls: Assuming f_s must always exceed twice the highest frequency (2 * 110 MHz = 220 MHz), ignoring bandpass undersampling techniques.
